subject: public.rcap_persons

findings.title: row level security is enabled on rcap_persons
findings.expectation: relrowsecurity = t with at least one policy

findings.title: anon holds no write privilege on rcap_persons
findings.expectation: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are all false

findings.title: authenticated holds no write privilege on rcap_persons
findings.expectation: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are all false

findings.title: an anonymous caller cannot read participant identities
findings.observed: anon read: we-must-vote -> email:participant@example.org | fulton-county -> name:jordan lee

findings.title: an anonymous caller cannot insert into a partner's keyspace
findings.observed: anon created person c2595277-142c-444e-afd1-b92a40cc489e under we-must-vote

findings.title: a browser role cannot rewrite an existing participant identity
one consumer cannot enumerate another consumer's person row
findings.expectation: an authenticated caller reads no other consumer's rows

findings.title: a consumer's row cannot be located from their auth user id alone
findings.expectation: the derived key does not resolve for another caller
findings.observed: a caller who knows the target's auth user id located 1 row(s) via the published derivation

findings.title: a partner admin cannot read other partners' people
findings.expectation: a partner-scoped caller sees only its own namespace
findings.observed: an authenticated caller reads 3 distinct partner namespaces

findings.title: a browser role cannot alter a partner's reported population
findings.expectation: the partner's distinct-people count is unchanged
findings.observed: anon deleted 1 person row(s); distinct people 1 -> 0

findings.title: forged person rows cannot move partner packet entitlement
findings.expectation: packet accounting derives from the ledger, which no browser role can write
findings.observed: the credit ledger is not part of this schema slice; accounting is unreachable from rcap_persons alone

findings.title: the resolver fails closed if the reserved slug becomes a real partner
findings.expectation: resolveConsumerPersonId checks partner_records and refuses on collision

findings.title: the reserved consumer keyspace cannot be written by a browser role
findings.expectation: the INSERT into the reserved namespace is refused
findings.observed: anon inserted ea2a242f-6a04-4c1b-9fcc-ffcf6d982e25 into the reserved consumer namespace

findings.title: same auth user resolves to one stable person key
findings.expectation: the derivation is deterministic for a given user

findings.title: a different auth user resolves to a different person key
findings.expectation: distinct users never share a match key

findings.title: the matter is derived from the Briefcase item, not the browser
findings.expectation: one item yields one stable, well-formed matter; distinct items differ

findings.title: the reserved namespace is a constant, not a partner slug

notes: rcap_persons is created by supabase/phase-30-rcap-person-identity.sql with no RLS, no policy and no grant. On Supabase, default privileges then give anon and authenticated full CRUD.
Partner match keys are 'email:<address>' or 'name:<full name>' (src/lib/rcap/person-identity.ts deriveRcapPersonMatchKey), so the table stores participant contact identity in near-plaintext.
Consumer rows added by src/lib/expungement-ai/consumer-identity.ts digest their key; that mitigation does not extend to the partner rows beside them.
Reporting counts distinct person_id on rcap_document_packets; person_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a person row silently removes packets from a partner's reported population.
